was: Okanogan-Wenatchee NF campground 38 miles up the Entiat River Road from US-97A, ~3,100 ft, in a valley recovering from wildfire. 25 first-come, first-served sites along the Entiat River; trailers up to 25 ft recommended, and the road can be rough in spots. Vault toilets and garbage service; no hookups. Trailheads into the Glacier Peak country beyond; Cottonwood Cabin next door is reservable. --Claude

was: Chequamegon-Nicolet NF campground between East and West Twin Lakes, 8 miles west of Washburn on the Bayfield Peninsula. 16 single-family sites for tents or RVs, 25-45 ft; both lakes have small boat access. No hookups. Some sites reservable, the rest first-come, first-served. Blueberry picking in the Moquah Barrens in late summer; Valhalla trails and the Long Lake beach nearby. --Claude

was: Large concession-run campground on the northwestern shore of Lake Berryessa, on Berryessa Knoxville Road half a mile north of Pope Canyon Road, about 45 minutes from Napa or Winters. Around 160 sites - tent-only, RV-or-tent and RV-only - most of them on the water, many with room to moor a boat below the site; some RV sites have electric for an extra fee. Boat and watercraft rentals. Reservable May 1 to October 1, first-come, first-served otherwise; open year-round. Extra-person, pet and vehicle fees apply. --Claude

was: Small Mendocino NF campground in an open oak grove above the North Fork of Stony Creek, about 10 miles west of Stonyford on paved Road 18N03 in the Fouts Springs OHV area. 10 sites, trailers to 30 ft; vault toilet, no drinking water, pack out trash, no hookups. First-come, first-served (scan-and-pay). --Claude

was: Eldorado NF campground off Ice House Road (FR 3, then FR 33) near Gerle Creek Reservoir, 5,300 ft. 16 tent/trailer/RV units with tables, fire rings and bear boxes; vault toilet, no water (bring your own), no hookups; dump station at the Loon Lake boat ramp. First-come, first-served, Memorial Day to mid-October. Popular with OHV riders heading for the Rubicon Trail. --Claude

was: Low-cost Corps of Engineers campground on the east shore of Fort Supply Lake in northwest Oklahoma, below the dam embankment. 16 open, grassy non-electric sites around a loop, several with shade shelters right by the water; vault toilet, boat ramp, swim beach down the road. No hookups. First-come, first-served (scan-and-pay). Crappie, walleye and catfish; sand dunes line the shore. --Claude
